Date: 2026-12-01
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Location: Zoom
Redwood hosts: Ben Fletcher, Riya Patel, Liam O'Connor
Sherpa hosts: Alex Romero, Priya Menon, Samir Gupta, Natalie King
Artifacts shared: QBR deck (drive: https://drive.redwood/sherpa-qbr-deck), benchmark sheet (sheet: https://sheets.red/sherpa-bench)
summary: Quarterly health review focused on usage spikes, cost levers, and stability. Customer is evaluating Dedicated capacity for predictable latency during peak windows and is concerned about token-level cost during high-volume jobs. Security/compliance gating (SOC2 + KMS) and private VPC feasibility were raised as blockers for a pilots. Agreed next steps: run a Dedicated latency baseline, share pricing scenarios with quantization, and schedule a deep dive on private deployment requirements.
transcript:
[00:00] Ben Fletcher: Alright folks thanks for joining, we'll kick off the Sherpa QBR. Quick who we have on deck?
[00:10] Alex Romero: Hey everyone, Alex here - Head of ML.
[00:15] Priya Menon: Priya, platform eng. Sorry I'm on mobile, little echo.
[00:20] Ben Fletcher: No worries. Riya and Liam from Redwood with me.
[00:26] Riya Patel: morning, afternoon—depending on your timezone. We'll go through usage, cost, stability and next steps.
[00:37] Liam O'Connor: Quick admin — deck and benchmark sheet links in the chat.
[00:44] Alex Romero: Got it, thanks.
[00:47] Ben Fletcher: Ok first slide, usage: Alex you had a big burst last month around product search rerank? Can you summarize what drove that?
[01:02] Alex Romero: Yeah so we rolled out a personalized reranker into search last month, traffic spiked during the launch and we saw a 3x increase in token volume for a 6 hour window. It was mostly evening traffic.
[01:20] Riya Patel: And that produced a latency tail that we flagged — 95th went from ~220ms to 480ms for the v1 model on Hosted.
[01:30] Priya Menon: Correct — the kv cache seemed to be warming badly. We had a few cold-start eviction cycles.
[01:38] Ben Fletcher: When you say kv cache, do you mean the prefix cache? Sometimes the transcript says K V cash, haha.
[01:44] Samir Gupta: yes prefix cache, sorry the notes use different terms.
[01:48] Ben Fletcher: No problem. So the big question — Dedicated reserved capacity would have smoothed that. Riya, can you explain the latency vs cost tradeoffs we reviewed?
[01:59] Riya Patel: Sure. Dedicated gives predictable compute and much tighter 95th percentile tails because you avoid noisy neighbor effects. Cost-wise, reserved Dedicated is higher committed spend but lower per-token during steady state. For bursty traffic you can combine Dedicated with burst pools—there's a tradeoff with how much idle capacity you accept.
[02:20] Natalie King: Our finance team is worried about the commit. Samir, comments?
[02:26] Samir Gupta: Yeah commit is the blocker. We need a clear model that shows ROI vs cost — especially if the burst is only 4-6 hours a week.
[02:35] Ben Fletcher: Understood. We suggested quantization plus batching to reduce token compute. In the pricing sheet I'll add a scenario: no quant vs 8-bit quant vs 4-bit quant.
[02:48] Alex Romero: For quality, 4-bit caused occasional hallucinations in our tests — need to see eval A/B.
[02:55] Riya Patel: That's expected. We'll include quality delta estimates and recommend a canary rollout with A/B evaluation via Redwood Console eval hooks.
[03:07] Priya Menon: On security — we need SOC2 docs and proof that logs can be exported to our SIEM. Also KMS integration is required for encryption at rest.
[03:18] Liam O'Connor: We can share SOC2 artifacts and the audit log export sample. KMS is supported for Private deployments and for Dedicated with customer-managed keys in some configurations.
[03:29] Alex Romero: Is that also true for Hosted? We prefer Hosted for day-to-day but security team may require VPC or Private.
[03:36] Ben Fletcher: Hosted supports envelope encryption but not full customer-managed KMS today. Private gives you KMS/HSM and full network control. We'll put a comparison matrix in the follow-up.
[03:48] Priya Menon: Another thing — we run on GCP and have strict egress rules. Can Private be air-gapped or at least VPC-peered?
[03:56] Riya Patel: Private can be VPC-peered; on-prem air-gapped options exist but require more lead time. We'll map the network diagram.
[04:04] Ben Fletcher: Ok slide for reliability incidents — you had a 2-hour degradation mid-November. Alex, can you walk us through root cause notes?
[04:12] Alex Romero: It was a combination of a model rollout and a config change that inadvertently increased sequence length. The runtime's kernel selection then moved to a slower path and KV cache thrash amplified it.
[04:28] Riya Patel: We recommended pinned model versions and canary rollouts — Redwood's rollout feature can auto-fallback when latency SLOs are breached.
[04:36] Priya Menon: That rollback saved us during one test, yes. Question — does Redwood provide tracing hooks for spans so our SREs can ingest them?
[04:46] Liam O'Connor: Yes, there are tracing hooks and per-request metadata you can pipe to your observability stack. We'll share examples for Datadog and OpenTelemetry.
[04:56] Samir Gupta: On cost — our main levers right now are batching, prefix cache tuning, and quantization. Any other quick wins?
[05:04] Riya Patel: Token preserialization, caching at the model gateway, and request coalescing for similar prompts. Also schedule-based warm pools that spin up before expected peaks.
[05:15] Alex Romero: About warm pools — how do we avoid paying for idle GPU time?
[05:20] Ben Fletcher: You can use a hybrid policy: reserved base Dedicated for steady load + burst on demand. Redwood Optimize will recommend autoscale thresholds and batching windows to minimize idle cost.
[05:32] Natalie King: Timeline question — if we wanted Dedicated in Q1, what's the lead time?
[05:37] Riya Patel: Usually 4–6 weeks from contract to provisioning for standard capacity, longer if you need private VPC or on-prem packaging.
[05:46] Priya Menon: We'll need an environment for benchmarking. Can Redwood run a 24-hour dedicated benchmark with our QPS profile?
[05:53] Riya Patel: Yes — we can run a Dedicated baseline. Riya (self-note) will run 95th percentile latency baseline on v1 during our next availability window.
[06:02] Ben Fletcher: Action item captured.
[06:05] Alex Romero: Good. Also, can we get a token-level breakdown by route? Our billing granularity right now is too coarse.
[06:13] Liam O'Connor: We'll enable per-route cost reporting in the Console for you and share a sample report.
[06:19] Samir Gupta: Wonderful. Back to security: any concerns about audit logs containing PII? We need redaction options.
[06:27] Liam O'Connor: We can redact payloads in logs and provide a redaction policy. We'll surface options in the SOC2 doc packet.
[06:35] Priya Menon: For private deployment feasibility — what dependencies do you need from our side?
[06:41] Riya Patel: Network diagram, expected QPS and sequence length distribution, security controls, and compliance checklist. Also point of contact for infra provisioning.
[06:51] Ben Fletcher: We'll send a requirements checklist after this call.
[06:54] Alex Romero: On a different note — competitor watch. We benchmarked an Anthropic endpoint last month and saw slightly lower latency on small models but higher cost. Worth keeping in the matrix.
[07:07] Riya Patel: Yep we included competitor rows in the pricing sheet.
[07:11] Natalie King: Ok can we recap next steps?
[07:15] Ben Fletcher: Sure. Liam?
[07:17] Liam O'Connor: I'll put the SOC2 docs and audit log sample into the drive link, share per-route cost report sample, and ping method for Datadog tracing.
[07:27] Ben Fletcher: Riya will run the Dedicated latency baseline and share results. I'll send the pricing scenarios and quantization cost projections. Priya will provide QPS profiles.
[07:37] Priya Menon: I'll send peak windows and sample traffic patterns.
[07:40] Samir Gupta: Finance will review the pricing scenarios once received.
[07:44] Ben Fletcher: Anything else?
[07:46] Alex Romero: One ask — include expected quality deltas for quantized models in the benchmark so we can set guardrails.
[07:54] Riya Patel: Will do, quality delta and A/B plan in the follow-up.
[07:58] Ben Fletcher: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the private-deploy deep dive.
[08:06] Natalie King: Thanks, bye.
[08:09] (call ends)

Notes: transcript includes a few mis-hearings (kv cache transcribed as K V cash in places). Occasional chuckles and crosstalk removed for clarity.
